bibliographic.title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence in Strengthening Risk Compliance and Driving Financial Innovation in Banking
bibliographic.venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
bibliographic.citation_apa: Paleti, S. (2022). The role of artificial intelligence in strengthening risk compliance and driving financial innovation in banking. International Journal of Science and Research, 11(12). https://doi.org/10.21275/SR22123165037

methodology.technology_context: General AI, machine learning, NLP, chatbots, generative AI, and large language models discussed within banking risk compliance, fraud detection, customer engagement, and regulatory compliance contexts

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article is a broad conceptual overview of AI for risk compliance and financial innovation in banking. Mentions of chatbots, NLP, generative AI, and large language models are brief and peripheral; it does not centrally address conversational governance of LLM-based systems.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper touches regulated banking, compliance, oversight, transparency, chatbots, generative AI, and large language models, its primary contribution is a general discussion of AI-enabled banking innovation and risk control rather than governance of conversational LLM systems. No dedicated study design, sample, or framework for conversational AI governance is presented in the provided text.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Metadata year (2021) conflicts with journal issue date (December 2022); abstract and several passages appear garbled or corrupted, limiting reliable appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual banking-AI overview without reported empirical methods, sampling, data collection, or systematic analysis. Provided excerpts do not describe study limitations or ethics. Text quality issues reduce confidence in full-text interpretation.

cerqual.explanation: Low confidence for the review topic because conversational governance of LLM systems is not a central or coherently developed focus; the paper offers only incidental mentions amid a general banking-AI narrative.

coding.theme: AI for risk compliance and innovation in banking
coding.subtheme: incidental references to chatbots, generative AI, and LLMs

synthesis.main_claim: Artificial intelligence can strengthen risk compliance and drive financial innovation in banking through applications such as fraud detection, customer engagement, real-time monitoring, and regulatory compliance support.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a broad conceptual framing of AI use in banking risk and innovation, with brief references to chatbots, generative AI, LLMs, and regulatory transparency requirements.
synthesis.limitations: No empirical evaluation; conversational governance and LLM-specific governance are not developed as core topics; provided text lacks clear methodological reporting and contains corrupted passages.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance in LLM-based regulated systems; at most marginal contextual background on banking AI regulation and brief technology mentions.

evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed journal article published in IJSR December 2022.

evidence.claim: Paper presents a conceptual overview of AI in banking rather than an empirical study.
evidence.excerpt: This paper outlines how Artificial Intelligence (AI) augmented intelligence is changing the way the banking sector is doing business today.

evidence.claim: Primary focus is AI for risk compliance and financial innovation in banking.
evidence.excerpt: The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) provides enhanced opportunities for financial innovation in banking, while concurrently promoting various forms of risk compliance in the financial services industry.

evidence.claim: Chatbots and NLP are mentioned as customer interaction AI, not as a governance focus.
evidence.excerpt: AI in the financial sector enables banks to deliver letters to customers via interaction AI by creating artificial chatbots that understand natural language processing.

evidence.claim: Large language models are mentioned only briefly in a customer personalization context.
evidence.excerpt: banks are likely to gain early mover's advantages by customizing through fine-tuning large language models to cater to the demands of individual customers

evidence.claim: LLMs are discussed as a risk example, not as an object of conversational governance.
evidence.excerpt: Large language models are an example of the newly developed AI technologies that promulgated misunderstanding and conspiracy theories on unprecedented scale in a matter of days.

evidence.claim: Generative AI governance is referenced in relation to AIA regulation and transparency, but not conversational governance specifically.
evidence.excerpt: Transparency in participation and executed practices is however a prerequisite to avoid that one side is profiting on another’s expense, which is regarded as essential in context of the AIA regulation due to generative AI applications.

evidence.claim: Paper discusses governing AI operations generally, including architecture, KPIs, testing, and troubleshooting.
evidence.excerpt: A comprehensive regime describing cohesively how AI (operations) work, with regard to architecture, KPIs, testing, and troubleshooting is another essential requirement.
